verdict.rationale: Working Copy's own docs say a private key can be generated inside the app and attached to an Identity, optionally kept on the Secure Enclave behind Face ID or Touch ID. The key authenticates Git over SSH, including to self-configured Linux, BSD and Synology servers, but the evidence only covers Git access, not general password-less server login. missing for 10: documented export or installation of the public key onto arbitrary servers (auto-registration is documented only for GitHub/BitBucket), evidence of password-less access beyond Git operations, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can generate SSH key pairs for password-less access to my servers

citations.quote: You attach a private key to your Identity which can be imported or generated inside the app.
For extra security SSH keys can reside on the Secure Enclave protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
your public key will automatically be registered with BitBucket or GitHub.
configure a regular Linux server, BSD server & Synology NAS to act as a hosting provider, using SSH commands for listing repositories.
